You are an expert medical researcher. Extract all clinical recommendations from the following clinical practice guideline text.

A "recommendation" is an actionable statement that directs clinical practice and is explicitly graded with a strength of recommendation and a level of confidence.

For each recommendation, extract:
- The recommendation text — copy it EXACTLY as written in the source
- The strength of recommendation — use ONLY these valid values: strong/conditional [for/against]
- The level of confidence — use ONLY these valid values: high/moderate/low/very low

Output format: one recommendation per line, using pipe delimiters:
recommendation text | strength of recommendation | level of confidence

Rules:
- Extract ONLY explicitly stated recommendations with a clear strength of recommendation and level of confidence
- Copy the recommendation text EXACTLY as written — do NOT paraphrase or summarize
- Do NOT extract: background statements, evidence summaries, section headers, or statements without an explicit strength of recommendation and level of confidence
- Do NOT infer or create recommendations that are not in the text
- If no recommendations are found, output exactly: NO_RECOMMENDATIONS_FOUND
- Do NOT include headers, row numbers, or any other text

Examples of correctly extracted recommendations:
ACP recommends that clinicians use bisphosphonates for initial pharmacologic treatment | Strong For | High
We suggest against the routine use of albumin for fluid resuscitation | Weak Against | Low


--- Guideline Text ---
Nonpharmacologic and Pharmacologic Treatments of Adults in
the Acute Phase of Major Depressive Disorder: A Living Clinical
Guideline From the American College of Physicians
Amir Qaseem, MD, PhD, MHA; Douglas K. Owens, MD, MS; Itziar Etxeandia-Ikobaltzeta, PharmD, PhD; Janice Tufte;
J. Thomas Cross, Jr., MD, MPH; and Timothy J. Wilt, MD, MPH; for the Clinical Guidelines Committee of the American
College of Physicians* †
Description: The purpose of this guideline from the American
College of Physicians (ACP) is to present updated clinical recom-
mendations on nonpharmacologic and pharmacologic interven-
tions as initial and second-line treatments during the acute phase
of a major depressive disorder (MDD) episode, based on the
best available evidence on the comparative beneﬁts and harms,
consideration of patient values and preferences, and cost.
Methods: The ACP Clinical Guidelines Committee based
these recommendations on an updated systematic review of
the evidence.
Audience and Patient Population: The audience for this
guideline includes clinicians caring for adult patients in the
acute phase of MDD in ambulatory care. The patient popula-
tion includes adults in the acute phase of MDD.
Recommendation 1a: ACP recommends monotherapy with ei-
ther cognitive behavioral therapy or a second-generation antide-
pressant as initial treatment in patients in the acute phase of
moderate to severe major depressive disorder (strong recom-
mendation; moderate-certainty evidence).
Recommenda
--- End of Text ---
